evidence: Places the octagon as regular; all 15 slopes are correct (I re-derived them exactly). Counts 3 vertical x 3 horizontal = 9 pairs and checks each of the 9 meeting points (vertices 2,4,6,8, interior points such as (sqrt2/2,0), and the center). Slopes -1 vs 1 give 3x2 = 6 pairs: two meet at vertices 3 and 5 (dot product 0) and four inside, at (+-0.5,+-0.5) and (0,0). Proves m4*m10 = -1 and m6*m12 = -1, with intersections (0.207,0.5) and (0.5,0.207), and rules out the other products. 9+2+6 = 17. My enumeration gives the same 17 pairs, all inside or on the boundary. Some vertex vectors are wrong (e.g. 2->6), but only for pairs that are not perpendicular.

Then 6 slope -1 x slope 1 pairs, plus 5-2/3-8 and 1-4/2-7, proving both products equal -1. Solves the intersections ((sqrt2-1)/2, 1/2), (1/2, 0.207), (-0.5,+-0.5), (0.5,0.5), (0,0), and the shared vertices 5 and 3. 9+8 = 17, matching my enumeration. It wrongly claims non-parallel chords always meet inside, but then checks each pair explicitly. Its early doubt that vertex angles can be 90 degrees is later corrected.
